Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
For a directed graph stored via adjacency lists, the cost of the operation on vertex v is simply its out-degree, i.e., the number of outgoing edges from v. The total cost over all |V| operations equals the sum of all out-degrees, which is exactly |E|.

* (a) The worst possible single operation costs |V| − 1, which occurs when a single vertex has outgoing edges to every other vertex in the graph.
* (b) By aggregate analysis, the average amortized cost is |E| / |V|, since the total cost across all |V| operations is |E| (each edge is counted exactly once as an outgoing edge of its source vertex).
